text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysia is to set up 85 "smart" schools by January 1, 1999, in order to produce students with analytical skills, said Education Minister Najib Tun Razak on Monday.
-- Sarawak state on the island of Borneo, has closed its border crossing posts with Kalimantan following racial tension in the Indonesian territory.
-- The Securities Commission announced several measures to strengthen the regulatory framework for unit trusts.
-- Foreign professionals who work illegaly while on social passes will be the Immigration Department's next target, said its deputy director general Aseh Che Mat.

-- Time Telecom Holdings Bhd will offer prospective investors in its proposed listing exercise a free mobile phone, its chairman Shamsir Omar said on Monday. The company is a unit of Time Engineering Bhd.
-- Bridgecon Bhd is to participate in infrastructure projects worth 500 million ringgit, including the new government administrative centre of Putrajaya.
